title: F3: daemon posts Codex results — _dispatch_worker turns executor.start()'s return into a bus result
spec:
Gotcha 2026-09-19: orchestrator/daemon.py _dispatch_worker() (about line 305) calls executor.start(task_id, prompt) and discards the returned dict, so a Codex-executed task stays running with pid null after its run logs done; three tasks needed hand-posted results. The Claude fallback path posts from spawn.run_worker and is unaffected. Change _dispatch_worker():
1. r = executor.start(...). status done -> bus.post_result(task_id, fit_result({summary: r['message'][:3000], executed_by: 'codex:' + executor id, thread: r['thread'], usage: r.get('usage')}), 'done'). status failed -> bus.post_result(..., 'failed') with reason. status held -> leave the hold executor set (it already updated the bus) and do nothing else. Use spawn.fit_result (or move it to bus if import order needs it) so the result stays within the bus size cap.
2. If executor.start raises, keep today's pipeline.dispatch_error stamp and also set the task failed with reason 'dispatch error: ...' so it never stays running.
3. The gate then treats the task like any other done execute task (tests-green, review policy, merge).
Tests in tests/test_daemon.py with executor.start monkeypatched: done posts a done result with executed_by codex:astra; failed posts failed with the reason; held leaves status held; a raising start marks the task failed. Keep every existing test green.
acceptance: Existing tests pass; .claude/hooks/tests-green.sh exits 0 in the worktree
